title: County of Foix
capsule: The County of Foix was a southern French fief centered on the city of Foix in the eastern Pyrenean foothills, whose counts emerged as significant lords from the eleventh century and gained particular notoriety during the Albigensian Crusade—Count Raymond-Roger de Foix was a staunch defender of Cathar communities against Simon de Montfort's forces after 1209. From 1278 the counts held the co-principality of Andorra jointly with the Bishop of Urgell, an arrangement that survives today. The most celebrated ruler, Gaston III 'Phoebus' (1331–1391), expanded the domain through the acquisition of Béarn, wrote the influential hunting treatise Livre de chasse, and maintained a brilliant court chronicled by Froissart. Through the inheritance of Henry of Navarre, the county came to the French Crown in 1607 and was merged into the Ariège département at the Revolution.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The county's boundaries are well attested through medieval charters and feudal surveys; the atlas end date of 1556 likely reflects the formal union with Béarn and Navarre under Henry II of Navarre rather than the 1607 union with France.
